items.evidence_text: For a patient starting treatment, eGFR from 30 through 45 is a range in which initiation is not recommended. Use becomes contraindicated only when eGFR is under 30.
items.candidate_claim: A treatment-naive patient with eGFR 38 is in the range where starting therapy is not recommended.

items.evidence_text: The initiation rule covers eGFR 30 to 45 as not recommended, whereas the contraindication rule applies below 30.
items.candidate_claim: An eGFR of 38 satisfies the contraindication rule.

items.evidence_text: For people already taking the medicine, kidney function below eGFR 45 calls for reassessing benefit against risk. The separate discontinuation threshold is below 30.
items.candidate_claim: An established user at eGFR 43 should undergo benefit-risk reassessment, not automatic discontinuation on the basis of that value alone.

items.evidence_text: In an existing user, eGFR below 45 triggers benefit-risk reassessment; stopping therapy is specified only below 30.
items.candidate_claim: An existing user with eGFR 43 must stop the medicine immediately because the value is below 45.

items.evidence_text: Concomitant NSAID exposure is associated with greater bleeding risk during anticoagulant therapy.
items.candidate_claim: The evidence supports an increase in bleeding risk when an NSAID is used with the anticoagulant.

items.evidence_text: The source identifies greater bleeding risk with an NSAID. It does not provide an across-the-board prohibition on the combination.
items.candidate_claim: The source proves that the NSAID-anticoagulant combination is absolutely prohibited for every patient.

items.evidence_text: NSAID co-exposure raises bleeding risk, but this evidence contains no comparison showing which age group has the greatest risk.
items.candidate_claim: NSAID co-exposure raises bleeding risk, and patients over 75 have the greatest risk of all age groups.

items.evidence_text: The warning states that treatment can precipitate a serious toxicity syndrome and that other agents acting through the same pathway can further increase that risk.
items.candidate_claim: The evidence supports a possible toxicity syndrome and greater risk when similar concomitant agents are present.

items.evidence_text: The toxicity syndrome is a possible serious event, but an isolated symptom does not establish the diagnosis in an individual patient.
items.candidate_claim: A single isolated symptom establishes that the patient has the toxicity syndrome.

items.evidence_text: Spontaneous reports can contribute to detecting a possible safety signal. Causal attribution cannot be established from an isolated spontaneous report alone.
items.candidate_claim: The reporting system can contribute to safety-signal detection while causal attribution remains unestablished.

items.evidence_text: A spontaneous report can suggest a signal, but an individual report cannot establish that the product caused the event.
items.candidate_claim: A single spontaneous report establishes that the product caused the event.

items.evidence_text: Spontaneous-report counts are affected by incomplete and selective reporting, so the observed count is not a measure of the true event incidence.
items.candidate_claim: The observed spontaneous-report count measures the true event incidence.

items.evidence_text: The registry lists the study as RECRUITING and identifies its prespecified primary endpoint. This record does not provide an efficacy outcome.
items.candidate_claim: The registry supports the recruiting status and the identity of the prespecified primary endpoint.

items.evidence_text: The registry marks the study as COMPLETED and gives the prespecified primary endpoint, but the supplied record does not show whether that endpoint was achieved.
items.candidate_claim: The study is completed and the registry identifies its primary endpoint, but this evidence does not establish that the endpoint was achieved.

items.evidence_text: The registry marks the study as COMPLETED and identifies the primary endpoint, but gives no evidence here that the endpoint was met.
items.candidate_claim: The study is completed and its primary endpoint was achieved successfully.

items.evidence_text: The registry supplies design and status information only; it contains no clinical-benefit result in the evidence provided here.
items.candidate_claim: The registration record proves that the investigational treatment provides clinical benefit.

items.evidence_text: Guideline F supersedes Guideline E as the current recommendation source.
items.candidate_claim: Guideline F is current, whereas Guideline E is no longer the current recommendation source.

items.evidence_text: Guideline F supersedes Guideline E for current recommendations.
items.candidate_claim: Guideline E remains the current recommendation source after Guideline F supersedes it.

items.evidence_text: Guideline F is current. The supplied evidence says nothing about whether an older Guideline D was ever superseded by F.
items.candidate_claim: Guideline F superseded Guideline D.

items.evidence_text: A new randomized study favors option Z, but the current guideline has not been revised and continues to recommend option S.
items.candidate_claim: There is new randomized evidence favoring Z, while the current guideline still recommends S.

items.evidence_text: New randomized evidence favors Z. The current guideline is unrevised and continues to recommend S.
items.candidate_claim: The publication automatically changes the current guideline recommendation from S to Z.

items.evidence_text: Drug U inhibits CYP3A and Drug V is a CYP3A substrate, providing a plausible pharmacokinetic interaction mechanism. No clinical management instruction is supplied in this evidence.
items.candidate_claim: The evidence supports a potential CYP3A-mediated pharmacokinetic interaction between U and V.

items.evidence_text: Drug U is a CYP3A inhibitor and Drug V is a CYP3A substrate. This evidence contains no dose-adjustment or contraindication instruction.
items.candidate_claim: The CYP3A mechanism alone establishes that U and V are clinically contraindicated together.

items.evidence_text: A genotype is associated with higher drug exposure, but the evidence does not specify a therapeutic dose recommendation.
items.candidate_claim: The genotype is associated with higher exposure, while the dose decision remains unresolved by this evidence.

items.evidence_text: The genotype is associated with higher exposure and the source gives no therapeutic dose recommendation.
items.candidate_claim: The genotype is associated with higher exposure, and every carrier therefore requires dose reduction.

items.evidence_text: An observational cohort found an association between exposure R and outcome T. The design is insufficient to establish a causal effect of R on T.
items.candidate_claim: The cohort supports an association between R and T without establishing causality.

items.evidence_text: An observational cohort found an association between R and T, and the study design is insufficient to establish causality.
items.candidate_claim: The cohort establishes that R causally produces T.

items.evidence_text: The imaging report describes the lesion as indeterminate and recommends MRI for further characterization. Malignancy is not established by the report.
items.candidate_claim: The lesion is indeterminate, and MRI is recommended for further characterization.

items.evidence_text: The report calls the lesion indeterminate, recommends MRI, and does not establish malignancy.
items.candidate_claim: The lesion is indeterminate and MRI is recommended, but the lesion is probably malignant.

items.evidence_text: The lesion is explicitly classified as benign in the report.
items.candidate_claim: The report classifies the lesion as malignant.

items.evidence_text: Two separate studies report response rates of 71% and 54% in different populations, without a randomized head-to-head comparison.
items.candidate_claim: The available studies report different response percentages, but they do not provide a randomized head-to-head superiority test.

items.evidence_text: Separate non-head-to-head studies report response rates of 71% and 54% in different populations. The percentages do not constitute a randomized superiority comparison.
items.candidate_claim: The larger percentage proves that treatment A is superior to treatment B.

items.evidence_text: The current label explicitly states that treatment A is contraindicated with condition B.
items.candidate_claim: The current label states that treatment A is contraindicated with condition B.

items.evidence_text: The current label explicitly states that treatment A is not contraindicated solely because of condition B.
items.candidate_claim: Condition B alone makes treatment A contraindicated according to this label.

items.evidence_text: This evidence entry contains no recommendation about whether treatment A should be used in condition B.
items.candidate_claim: Treatment A is contraindicated in condition B.

items.evidence_text: The evidence supports association A with outcome B, but provides no information about whether subgroup C has stronger association than subgroup D.
items.candidate_claim: The evidence supports association A with B, and subgroup C has a stronger association than subgroup D.
